subject: Critical Thinking
title: What Is Ethics? Morality Beyond 'Just Follow the Rules'
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on What Is Ethics? Morality Beyond 'Just Follow the Rules'.

hook.text: A child asks: 'Why is stealing wrong?' You answer: 'Because it's the rule.' They ask: 'But who made the rule?

buildup.text: Ethics is the philosophical study of right & wrong – not just WHAT the rules are, but WHY they exist & whether they're.

discovery.text: Three main approaches: consequentialism, deontology, virtue ethics. Each answers 'why' differently.

twist.text: No single framework solves every dilemma. That's not a bug – it's the nature of moral complexity.

climax.text: Ethics doesn't give you answers. It gives you better questions and more rigorous ways to think about them.

punchline.text: Rules tell you what to do. Ethics tells you why — and when to break them.

quiz.question: What are the three main approaches to ethics?

details.summary: Ethics is a systematic inquiry into right and wrong that goes far beyond obeying laws or social customs. It asks why certain actions are right and builds frameworks for evaluating moral questions on their own terms.
details.whyItMatters: Without ethical reasoning, people default to habit or authority and cannot defend or question the rules they follow.
takeaways: Ethics examines reasons behind moral rules
Legality and morality are not the same

faq.question: How does ethics differ from simply following societal rules?
faq.answer: Rules tell you what to do; ethics asks why you should do it. A rule can be unjust, and ethics provides the tools to recognize and challenge that injustice.

faq.question: Why should someone study ethics if they already try to be good?
faq.answer: Good intentions can lead to bad outcomes without a framework for evaluating consequences, duties, and values. Studying ethics sharpens your ability to navigate ambiguity.
